archetype.name: Point Guard (play-action distributor)
archetype.definition: A rhythm passer who runs Shanahan's under-center, play-action offense by hitting whichever of Kittle, McCaffrey, Evans or Samuel the concept frees, and who adds value by scrambling when the play breaks down.

report.headline: Purdy is near his 2023 peak, but Minnesota's pass rush tests the protection.
report.take:
Purdy is having one of the best passing seasons in the league again. His 0.304 EPA per dropback ranks 4th of 54, his 8.97 yards per attempt ranks 3rd, and he sits 7.7 points of CPOE above the qualifier average. This looks a lot like 2023, when he led the league at 0.338 EPA per play, more than his merely good 2024. Compared with last year he is gaining more per throw (yards per attempt up 1.34) and throwing interceptions half as often per game (down 0.56), while his completion rate over expected is a touch lower. He is getting the ball out a bit quicker and pushing it a little further.

The engine is the scheme meeting accuracy. On throws of 0-9 air yards he completes 80.7% at +8.5 CPOE for 0.392 EPA a throw and 11 touchdowns. Under center, the play-action looks, his success rate is 0.621 with +15.1 CPOE. Shanahan's offense manufactures easy completions and Purdy hits them on time. Pass protection helps too: he is pressured on only 15.8% of dropbacks (6th lowest) and the 49ers rank 3rd in hit rate allowed. When plays do break, his 21 scrambles have produced 0.87 EPA each and 13 first downs. That matters more than his designed runs, which average 1.67 yards a carry.

The headline numbers hide two things. First, a lot of the explosiveness has come from a small number of throws and one receiver. Twenty-four deep attempts produced 0.991 EPA apiece. Mike Evans' 0.873 EPA per target on 40 targets is the biggest single contribution in the passing game, and Evans is currently listed Out with Achilles tendinitis. Second, the protection that carried the first month has slipped. He took zero sacks in the first four games, and all 13 of his sacks have come in the last five, with a 7.9% sack rate in that stretch. Over those five games his EPA per dropback falls to 0.194. That is still good, but it is clearly worse than the season mark.

The floor here is real. He has been an efficient, accurate system passer for four seasons, and red-zone touchdowns (13 with no interceptions) plus a top-ranked offense keep his production stable. What will move is the ceiling. The deep-ball efficiency and the touchdown rate will cool, and his weekly output will depend more on Evans' health and on whether the sacks keep piling up.

strengths.title: Accuracy inside the scheme's timing
strengths.body: His short and intermediate game produces efficiency in volume rather than a few lucky hits. On throws under 10 air yards he completes 80.1% at +6.6 CPOE. Under center his success rate is 0.621 with +15.1 CPOE, because play-action pulls linebackers and he throws on rhythm into the space it creates. He showed the same trait in 2023 and 2025, so this should last.

strengths.title: Red-zone and late-game finishing
strengths.body: Inside the 20 he has 13 touchdown passes, no interceptions and +14.6 CPOE, and he has been sharper still in close fourth quarters (0.647 EPA a play). A red-zone touchdown rate like this always comes down some. Even so, a compressed field suits a quarterback who wins with timing and placement more than arm talent.

strengths.title: Scrambles that convert
strengths.body: He is no designed runner (1.67 yards a carry on those). As an off-script escape valve, though, his 21 scrambles average 0.87 EPA and have produced 13 first downs. Those plays offset a good share of what pressure costs him, and his rushing per game is up 8.3 yards on last year.

concerns.title: Sacks have arrived in bunches
concerns.body: He took no sacks through Week 4. Since then he has taken every one of his 13, a 7.9% rate over the last five games, including five in a shootout against the league's 32nd-ranked defense. His time to throw is down from last year, so this looks less like him holding the ball and more like protection slipping against better fronts. It matters most this week, against the league's best pass rush.

concerns.title: Explosive plays lean on Evans
concerns.body: Evans' 0.873 EPA per target is the biggest single contribution in the passing game. The 24 deep attempts at 0.991 EPA apiece are a small sample running well above any sustainable rate. With Evans listed Out, his availability largely decides whether the vertical game holds up or Purdy goes back to a Kittle-and-McCaffrey distributor.

concerns.title: Intermediate throws carry the turnover risk
concerns.body: Interceptions have been his career blemish (11, 12 and 10 in the last three seasons, all ranked near the bottom). This year is better, with a 1.9% interception rate. Three of his five picks have come on 10-19 yard throws, where his CPOE is flat at -0.3, and his bad-throw rate is up 1.3 points on last year. Over the last three games his interception rate is up 1.3 points as well.

trend.note: His game EPA has swung with opponents: big games against Miami, Arizona and Dallas, and a flat Week 5-7 stretch against Seattle, Washington and Atlanta (-0.8, 2.5, 2.5). The last two games rebounded strongly, but the sack count has risen throughout.

nextGame.headline: The league's top pass defense, against an offense missing its QB
nextGame.body:
Minnesota's defense is the worst matchup on the board for him. It ranks 1st in pass EPA allowed, 1st in success rate, 1st in QB hit rate and 1st in sack rate (12%), and it allows quarterbacks just 8.7 PPR points a game, the fewest in the league. It is also tough on tight ends (TE1s at -0.21 EPA a target, 2nd), which takes away Kittle. The openings are deep, where it ranks only 12th at 0.258 EPA, and lead receivers, who have averaged 0.44 EPA a target against it (27th). That fits Purdy's best throws, but only if Evans plays and the line holds up long enough for him to take them.

Availability tilts the game script toward a grind. The Vikings' offense already ranks 30th in EPA, and they are listed without Kyler Murray, Jordan Addison, Jauan Jennings and T.J. Hockenson. San Francisco should control the game as a 3-point favorite with a 46.5 total, which means fewer must-pass downs. Offenses already run against Minnesota more than any defense in the league (-9.6 pass rate over norm). On defense, LB Blake Cashman (95% of snaps) and DE Tyrion Ingram-Dawkins are out, which helps the middle-of-field play-action game. Van Ginkel is expected to practice. On Purdy's side, Evans being 'hoped' back at practice is the swing. An early forecast shows a drizzle chance and gusts near 18 mph, worth monitoring but not decisive.

keyMatchups.title: Minnesota's rush vs his protection
keyMatchups.body: The best sack-rate defense meets a quarterback who has taken all 13 of his sacks in the last five games. If the 49ers lean on under-center play-action, where his success rate is 0.621, they can slow that rush down. Shotgun obvious-passing downs are where this matchup gets ugly.

keyMatchups.title: Deep shots vs Minnesota's soft spot
keyMatchups.body: Minnesota is stingy on short throws but only middling deep. Purdy's 24 deep attempts have been his most efficient throws by far. Whether he can test that weakness depends heavily on Evans.

keyMatchups.title: Run-heavy game script
keyMatchups.body: A depleted Vikings offense and a run-funnel defense point to a 49ers lead and plenty of McCaffrey. That limits Purdy's attempts, as in his 22-throw Miami win, without necessarily hurting his efficiency.

nextGame.watch: Whether Evans practices this week, and how many times Purdy is sacked before halftime.

restOfSeason.body:
The base of this season is sustainable: four years of system accuracy, a top-ranked offense and the No. 1 passing EPA unit, a career-best interception rate, and a coach who keeps building easy throws for him. The parts that will regress are the deep-ball efficiency, the red-zone touchdown rate and some of the yards per attempt that rode on Evans' 0.873 EPA per target. Expect something closer to 2025-level efficiency than to the current pace, which still makes him a top-10 passer.

The bigger variable is protection. If the sack spike since Week 5 keeps going, the dropback EPA drifts toward the 0.194 of his last five games. If it settles, he stays near 0.25-0.30. Healthy receivers and favorable game scripts should keep him around 245-275 passing yards and roughly two touchdowns a game, with 15-25 rushing yards from scrambles.
swingFactors: Pass protection vs the sack spike

confidence.note: Nine strong starts and a consistent career profile, but the deep and red-zone splits are small and Evans' status is unsettled.
